findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed that the handwashing sink in the serving kitchen had no hot water, only cold water (the hot water lever produced no water when turned). CORRECTED: PIC removed the handwashing sink from service and instead re-designated the triple sink in the serving kitchen for handwashing only until the handwashing sink can be repaired. The triple sink does have both hot and cold water. All warewashing of utensils and equipment from the serving kitchen will instead be done in the main kitchen which has adequate equipment for warewashing. Ensure that handwashing sinks are equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 85 F.
findings.citation_text: 5-202.12(A) Handwashing Sink, Installation. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 29.4°C (85°F) through a mixing valve or combination faucet. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed a mop in the main cooking kitchen that was stored in the bottom basin of the mop bucket in water where it cannot properly air-dry. CORRECTED: PIC moved the mop to the upper basket where the mop can effectively air-dry between uses. Ensure that mops are stored properly so that they can air-dry and not attract pests or mildew.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the facility’s chemical dish sanitizing machine to not be dispensing Cl (0-10 ppm) bleach after multiple runs. CORRECTED- The facility re-primed the machine and replaced the sanitizing solution. The sanitizer was observed to properly be dispensing a sanitizer solution at 200 ppm. Use the facility’s test strips to ensure that chemical dish machines used for sanitation of food contact surfaces are dispensing at a concentration of 50-200 ppm.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the handle of the ice scoop (intended for drinks) to be touching the ice. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) placed a metal container for storage of the ice scoop. Ensure food contact surfaces with handles are stored with the handles above or separate from the food to prevent accidental bare-hand contamination of food.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container. [C]

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
5-205.15: The piping under the garbage disposal is leaking where the water leaves the garbage disposal. Repairs need to be made by a licensed plumber. Due to the facility not being in operation during normal business hours, a follow-up of the plumbing is being set for January 9th, 2024 at 10am to ensure its repairs have been made and the plumbing has been brought into compliance. 
5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: The following areas will need repaired to create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface:
-The wood blocks being used to hold up the fridge need to be painted/sealed.
-The floor behind the equipment in the main kitchen needs to have coving placed or some other method to effectively seal the floor to the wall.
-The floor in the second kitchen needs new coving or another method to effectively seal the floor to the wall where the gap is present, especially near the hand sink.
Ensure repairs are made to make these areas smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable.
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: There is an accumulation of dust/food debris in the following locations:
-The air vents/lightbulb case of the hood above the stove
-The air output of the dish machine hood
-The surface of the coffee maker where the water is expelled has a build up of coffee debris and needs wiped down.
Ensure these surfaces receive proper attention to be cleaned and sanitized and then cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
The trays leading into and out of the dish machine have gaps between tray backsplashes and wall.  Seal the gaps.

750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
The chlorine sanitizer in the dish machine was too weak to register on the test strips.   The bottle of sanitizer was changed and the dish machine was run until the concentration observed on the final rinse cycle was 100 ppm.   Maintain a chlorine concentration of 50-100 parts per million chlorine in the machine.

750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
The blade of the can opener and its table mount were soiled.  Clean and sanitize the can opener and mount.

750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The inside bottom of the cabinet below the tea brewing machine was soiled.  Clean the cabinet.

750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Some bowls and pans on the wire shelves in the room with the washer/dryer were stored food side up.  Invert the bowls and pans.

750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
1.  Coffee filters were stored unprotected near the coffee makers.  The filters were put in a zip lock bag to CORRECT the violation.
2.  A box of single service cups was setting on the floor in the supply room at the corner of the kitchen.  Store the box at least 6 inches above the floor.                       750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 1.  The corner of the floor under the dish machine was soiled.  (REPEAT VIOLATION)   Clean the floor.                2.  The coving under the dish machine does not join up under the dish machine.  (REPEAT VIOLATION)  Seal the coving so there is no gap between the two pieces.             3.  There is a gap between the floor and wall under/behind the wire shelves in the room with the washer/dryer.  (REPEAT VIOLATION)  Seal the gap or put coving over the joint.                   750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean.     750-1200  All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
A mop was stored in the mop bucket.  Store the mop hanging with the head up so the head will air dry.

750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.
